title: Davenport Bix festival and the leg aneurysm
summary: Chauncey played the Davenport Bix festival with Bill Challis, then suffered a severe leg pain diagnosed as an aneurysm and rushed back to New York.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: And out of that and through our association and then Chauncey in August of that same year. And he was at the Bix Festival. He had gone with Bill Challis to the Bix Festival in Davenport.
You and Bill Challis had gone there. And I was very hurt because....
Okay. That's the one I missed.
The first one is the one I missed.

He had been on his feet from 8:30 in the morning until about 12'30 at night, you know. And he had this terrible pain in his leg. And I remember he called me and he said I have the worst pain. He had to go to a doctor. He said right away. Then he called me back. He said after he had gone, Bill Challis had taken him to a doctor, called a doctor for him.
In Davenport. And the doctor, he was in such agony that he couldn't go to the hospital. The doctor said I'm afraid the leg is going to have to be amputated, which upset him terribly.
So he said all he could think about was getting back to New York. And so I called his daughter.
Aneurism. Do you know what an aneurism is?
So that was a whole tragic affair that took place. Suzy, I had just talked to her on the
phone and had met Chauncey's daughter, Suzy. But she got some very fine Doctors in New York City there. And it was a student doctor of DeBakey.
